evidence: Publil. Sent. B 1: ultrō sī offerās
Vulg. Lc. 24.42: obtulērunt eī partem piscis assī
terms.comment: ultrō offerre, to offer unasked; sē offerre, to present oneself or put oneself forward.

terms.gloss: offer (a post, an honour, a task) to someone
evidence: Caes. BG 2.4.7: ad hunc … summam tōtīus bellī omnium voluntāte dēferrī
Caes. BG 1.42.2: nōn respuit condiciōnem Caesar
M-O s.v. deal, terms (of agreement), settlement offer
terms.comment: alicui condiciōnem ferre, to make someone an offer (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Bis est grātum quod opus est, ultrō sī offerās.
phrases.english: What is needed is twice as welcome if you offer it unasked.

phrases.latin: Habētis hīc aliquid quod mandūcētur? At illī obtulērunt eī partem piscis assī et favum mellis.
phrases.english: Have you anything here to eat? And they offered him a piece of grilled fish and a honeycomb.

phrases.latin: Nōn respuit condiciōnem Caesar jamque eum ad sānitātem revertī arbitrābātur, cum id quod anteā petentī dēnegāsset ultrō pollicērētur.
phrases.english: Caesar did not reject the offer, and thought the man was coming to his senses, since he was now offering of his own accord what he had refused when asked.

sources: Lewis & Short: offero · Lewis & Short: defero · Lewis & Short: condicio
